t.E203.agn: The EU removed calcium sorbate from the list of authorised additives in 2018. The reason was that sufficient data on genotoxicity had not been submitted; this is a lack of data, not proven harm. The other sorbates (E200, E202) are authorised.
t.E203.body: In the body, sorbic acid is broken down (oxidised) in a similar way to other fatty acids such as caproic acid and is used as a source of energy.
t.E203.eff.0.t: Removed from the EU authorised list because genotoxicity data were not submitted; no proven harm, data are missing
t.E203.eval: Removed from the EU list of food additives on 12 August 2018; the reason is the lack of sufficient genotoxicity data (not proven harm, but missing data).
t.E203.found.0: Not authorised in the EU since 2018
t.E203.prod: Sorbic acid and its salts are produced by chemical synthesis; sorbic acid also occurs naturally in rowan berries.
t.E203.summary: The calcium salt of sorbic acid; a preservative used against moulds and yeasts.
t.E203.what: It was a preservative that slows the growth of moulds and yeasts.
t.agency.EU_withdrawn_2018: Removed from the authorised list in the EU.
